text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD
- Austria's social partners, the employers' and employees' representatives, are both strictly against a proposal of Social Democrat general secreatry Andreas Rudas to loosen the ban on Sunday work.
- Former Chancellor Franz Vranitzky, OSCE's special envoy to Albania, has spoken to the country's president Sali Berisha and plans to visit Albania soon.
- Carinthia's Social Democrats fear losing their majorities in Sunday's municipal elections in the southern Austrian state.

- The OECD's latest report on Austria said the government's austerity package would enable the country to meet the Maastricht budgetary criteria. However it harshly criticised the state run health and pension systems as too costly.
- Foreign workers in Austria are net payers to the country as Austria earns 10 billion schillings a year from them.
- The gas industry is strictly against the EU's plans to liberalise the market.
- Insurer EA Generali' profits were up 25 percent to 600 million schillings in 1996, as premium earnings jumped to a record high.
DIE PRESSE

- Conservative Family Affairs Minister Martin Bartenstein, demands a reduction of taxes in 1999, saying "Austrians have a right to this". This goes against the Finance Minister's plans to reform the country's tax system in the year 2000.
- Telephone call prices will be increased at peak times while the overall prices will fall, latest plans by state-owned Post & Telekom Austria reveal.
- The merging of GiroCredit and Die Erste savings bank activities is possible within the year, after the latter officially takes over GiroCredit.
- Steelmaker VA Stahl is looking for a strategic partner in eastern Europe and may have found it with the Czech Republic's Nova Hut.
- The latest studies on holiday plans by Austrians and Germans mean that Austria's ailing tourism industry could improve a little this year.

- Employees' union boss Hans Sallmutter demands the industry pay for the government's austerity measures. - Plastics producer Semperit's pre-tax profits rose 43 percent to 162 million schillings due to the successful expansion abroad of the company, its chief executive Zellner says.
KURIER
- Social Democrat and conservative pensioner representatives want pensions to be slowly increased above the inflation rate in 1998.
- Insurer EA-Generali plans to expand its cooperation with Die Erste savings bank, as its main partner Creditanstalt was taken over by Bank Austria.
- OECD expects Austria's unemployment to rise until next year, when the economy should improve.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- Bank Austria has granted Die Erste savings bank a free hand in Austria's savings bank sector, and says it will not take over any more savings banks.
